layers.note: Scattered stems among the sedges and mosses of bogs, fens and seeps, rarely many together.

moisture.note: Wet ground all season: bogs, fens, spongy places and seepages (PNW Flowers), wet meadows, stream edges and swampy coniferous forests (a University of Washington restoration protocol), as search results quote them.

heat_load.note: Any aspect where the ground stays wet; cool sites more often than hot ones.

elevation_m.note: Near sea level in the north to the subalpine in the western mountains (an Oregon specimen from a wet meadow at 1,806 m); the upper limits are loose.

shade_tolerance.note: Mostly open wetlands, but also swampy coniferous forest.

coldest_c.note: From maritime coasts to the boreal interior of Alaska and Canada: coldest-month means from about −25 °C (gone by −35 °C).

hard_freeze_c.note: A boreal perennial dormant underground in winter: lows to about −50 °C borne.

warmest_c.note: Cool summers: warmest-month means from about 9 to 22 °C, from subarctic and subalpine wetlands to mountain bogs in the south of its range; gone above about 26 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 900 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 500: short northern and subalpine seasons.

degree_days_5.note: About 300 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 100.

moisture_index.note: Wetlands fed by ground water and snowmelt even in dry regions, so almost no lower limit on the climate's own moisture.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit; its range takes in summer-dry coasts and mountains with summer rain, to about 0.7 of the year's precipitation.

provenance.notes: Climate ranges (niche schema 2): white bog orchid grows from the Komandor Islands across Alaska and Canada to the northern United States and south in the western mountains to northern Baja California (POWO and a University of Washington protocol, as search results quote them; the pages themselves were not read). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
